areas_reviewed: Compared T-PLAN.md section 10 with the shipped design-system section, Theme and Reuse rows, and plan amendments.
Reviewed the complete git diff 425a957..HEAD -- .claude docs, including phase invocation, remediation, precedence documentation and examples.
areas_not_reviewed: Pilot source file and original experimental artifacts outside this checkout; the tested rule was assessed from section 10's quotation.
Live generator behavior, Claude Code execution and empirical effects of the amended rule.
Engine and hook implementation outside the requested diff; no tests were executed.

findings.claim: The comparison incorrectly states that none of the additions changes what the generator is told to do with theme values: the added precedence rule explicitly changes that instruction when sources conflict.
findings.evidence: Section 10 quotes the tested rule as making the document "the source of this work's interface conventions" and directing "keep that meaning" for colours. The shipped ui-design.md instead says: "When it conflicts with something above it, the higher source wins and you raise the conflict with the user". This addition is correctly traced to section 8 item 2, but it instructs the generator to override conflicting theme values or meanings. Consequently section 10's assertion that "none of them changes what the generator is told to do with the theme's values" is false without a no-conflict qualification.
findings.suggested_fix: Qualify the equivalence statement to cases without higher-priority conflicts, and record precedence as an intentional, plan-authorized semantic exception whose effect the pilot did not test.
